whatChanged.title: Advanced packaging and memory bottlenecks gained visibility
whatChanged.detail: The quarter emphasized supply-chain constraints and capacity additions rather than generic chip cycle commentary.

whyItMatters.summary: Semiconductors stay structurally central when the bottleneck shifts from demand narrative to supply-chain reality, packaging, and manufacturing constraints.
statements: A good brief should separate broad AI enthusiasm from semiconductor-specific constraints.
Packaging, foundry capacity, and HBM references are stronger structural signals than headline AI demand alone.

requiredClaims: The brief should mention at least one bottleneck or capacity lane specific to semiconductors.
Relative share inside technology-general should remain high or strengthen.
provenanceExpectations: Use company commentary and supply-chain reporting to ground bottleneck claims.
notes: Do not let broad AI language replace chip-specific evidence.

subtopicMovement.rationale: Packaging and integration constraints are increasingly central to the narrative.
Memory bandwidth and HBM allocation remain key bottleneck signals.

pathways.note: Foundry capacity and packaging expansion are strong anchor evidence.
Equipment constraint and node transition evidence can validate long-horizon importance.

risks.title: AI spillover contamination
risks.detail: Chip coverage can look strong simply because AI is strong, even when semiconductor-specific constraints did not change.

watchpoints.trigger: Capacity expansion stories repeat across foundry, memory, and packaging lanes
watchpoints.implication: The theme is supported by real supply-chain stress rather than single-firm commentary.

prompts: Which semiconductor bottleneck now best explains the quarter's change in share?

notes: This file is designed to catch brief generations that describe semiconductors only as an AI beneficiary theme.
